extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and attorneys subject to USPTO professional conduct rules
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements used by the USPTO (OED and Director) to evaluate disciplineable conduct by registered patent attorneys and to impose sanctions (suspension, probation, publication, etc.). Includes substantive professional-conduct rules and procedural steps for probation violations and publication of orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect of a legal matter entrusted to counsel (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that, based on the stipulated facts, she violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) by neglecting a legal matter entrusted to her.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neglecting a client's patent matter (e.g., failing to provide a complete response to a § 103 rejection, failing to follow through on agreed communications or examiner interviews) constitutes a violation of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility. This provision was applied to the facts in this Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate designation of status identifier in filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The response prepared and filed by Respondent received Notices of Non-Compliant Amendment due to 'failing to accurately designate a status identifier.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filings must accurately designate the required status identifiers; failure to do so can render amendments non-compliant and subject the practitioner to discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper formatting of claim amendments (strikethrough and underline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The response to the Office Action failed to 'indicate amendments to the claims utilizing the strikethrough and underline format,' resulting in Notices of Non-Compliant Amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When amending claims, practitioners must use the prescribed strikethrough/underline convention so the Office can identify changes; failure to use required formatting may lead to non-compliance notices and disciplinary consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of certificates of mailing / filing method certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent 'cut-and-pasted' certificates of mailing from prior submissions, did not update them, and as a result signed and filed inaccurate certificates of mailing, incorrectly certifying filings as via EFS Web when they were actually filed via U.S. mail and/or facsimile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates of mailing/filing must truthfully and accurately reflect the method of transmission. Reusing template certificates without updating the method is an improper practice and may be treated as misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honoring fee arrangements and not charging contrary to agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent agreed to assist in drafting a complete response free of charge but later 'charged her client for assisting him' in preparing the response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must honor agreed fee arrangements or obtain informed consent for changes. Charging a client despite an explicit agreement to provide services free of charge is improper and may be disciplineable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fulfilling commitments to client communications and examiner contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent offered to send a status letter to the examiner and to conduct an examiner interview, the client agreed, but Respondent did not send the status letter and did not conduct the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representations to clients about actions (e.g., sending status letters, conducting interviews) should be followed through or the client should be promptly informed and given alternatives. Failure to follow through can constitute neglect or lack of diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful use and updating of template documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent 'used a prior form document as a template' that contained a certificate stating 'Mail or EFS' and in small print indicated EFS web; Respondent failed to notice/modify the EFS web language when mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on templates, practitioners must verify and update all template fields (including hidden/smaller-print portions) to ensure accuracy. Blindly copying template language that misstates filing methods or substantive facts is an anti-pattern that can produce incorrect certifications and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Billing accuracy and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Respondent worked over 20 hours on the matter, she 'only billed the client for four hours' and earlier charged the client despite an earlier agreement to provide certain work free of charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should maintain accurate time and billing records and ensure that billing reflects agreed arrangements. Inaccurate or misleading billing practices may aggravate disciplinary assessments even if not separately charged as a rule violation here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complying with probation conditions (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the agreed sanction Respondent 'shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58' and will serve a six-month probationary period commencing on reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions of probation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 are mandatory; failure to comply may trigger show-cause proceedings and further suspension. Practitioners under probation must adhere to all listed probation conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED obligations on probation supervision (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director 'shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59' in administering and supervising Respondent's probation and related procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED must follow the regulatory procedures for probation supervision and for initiating further disciplinary action when probationary conditions are violated, including providing required notices and records to the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall 'promptly to dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO Customer Numbers and Public Key Infrastructure ("PKI") certificates' and Respondent 'shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number unless and until she is reinstated.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon suspension or limited recognition, the practitioner’s electronic credentials and customer associations should be revoked or dissociated to prevent unauthorized practice; practitioners must not attempt to re-obtain access while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for addressing probation violations (Order to Show Cause; 15-day response; possible suspension up to six months)
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED believes Respondent failed to comply during probation, OED shall: (i) issue an Order to Show Cause why Respondent should not be suspended up to six months; (ii) send the Order to the Respondent at record address; and (iii) grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond. After considering any response, OED may deliver the Order, Respondent's response, and supporting argument to the USPTO Director to request immediate suspension for up to six months. Any review of such suspension does not postpone the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disciplinary process for probation violations requires formal notice, an opportunity to respond (15 days), and submission of records to the Director to seek further suspension; practitioners should be aware that seeking review of a resultant suspension will not stay the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of disciplinary orders and Notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall 'publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room' and 'publish the following notice in the Official Gazette: Notice of Suspension and Probation' (text describing the misconduct and sanction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary sanctions and the factual bases for them will be publicly posted and published; practitioners should expect public disclosure of the Final Order and summary notice in the Official Gazette as part of the sanctioning process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of prior discipline and use of record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding (including the Final Order) when addressing further complaints or in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent as an aggravating factor or to rebut any representation by Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner's prior disciplinary history may be used to aggravate sanctions or to rebut later claims; settlements or prior orders remain part of the disciplinary record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable professional conduct rules depend on timing of conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.20–10.112 vs. 11.101–11.901)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the alleged conduct occurred prior to May 3, 2013, the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.20–10.112) is applicable; Effective May 3, 2013, the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101–11.901) apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Which set of professional conduct rules governs alleged misconduct depends on when the conduct occurred; practitioners should apply the correct regulatory version when assessing alleged violations or defenses.
